rules: Both score bands are widened (+0.08 half-width in the engine); the score itself is never cut.
Output wording is 'your leanings now' — no labels, no 'types'.
An interest retest is scheduled in 6-12 months as part of the product (interest stability at 18-24 is ~0.67-0.70 — Low et al. 2005).
A direct verdict may NOT rest on interest convergence alone for <25: it requires a measured profession trial for the candidate AND at least one finished attempt in stage 1 (behavioural trace).

cddq_routing.classification_rule: Each of the 3 items votes for one type via the chosen option's `votes_for`. The type with the most votes wins. Tie-break order: inconsistent_information > lacks_information > not_ready (a tie means at least some conflict/lack is present, and not_ready only wins when it is the outright majority).

cddq_routing.purpose: Classify the user's career-decision difficulty type BEFORE stage 0 (structure after Gati, Krausz & Osipow 1996; the CDDQ questionnaire text itself is all-rights-reserved and is NOT used — these are our own items). The type routes the interview and the presentation; it never changes scores.

inconsistent_information.label: Inconsistent information
inconsistent_information.route: Standard route with extra weight on stages 2, 3 and 5; the contradiction mirror (stage 5) is built BEFORE final scoring.

lacks_information.label: Lacks information
lacks_information.route: Standard route through stages 0-6, with extra weight on stage 1 (history) and the RJP 'Day in the profession' module.

not_ready.label: Not ready
not_ready.route: Coaching block and small steps first; deep diagnostics is not forced. Scoring mode is forced to insufficient_data until readiness changes.

stages.free_prompt_hint: Read the candidate's real Tuesday out loud — including the boring and the worst parts, no selling. Then ask the anchored question per candidate and record the answer exactly; do not argue with a 'not mine'.
stages.purpose: Each top candidate is checked against a realistic day vignette (routine, people, paperwork, the worst parts — 'could you live 200 of these Tuesdays?'), then the person self-reports perceived fit per candidate. Perceived fit is the person's own gut vote on a real day: 'not_mine' REMOVES the candidate from the matches and the slot refills with the next candidate; 'mine' gives a small, bounded LOVE nudge (+0.05) so a called-mine profession outranks an unmarked equal (founder QA rule, 27.10.2026 — supersedes the Day-1 veto-only reading of Kristof-Brown et al. 2005 / Edwards 2008)..
